test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 17 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to GS Krishnan, which of the following sectors are highlighted in the India BioEconomy Report, 2025?

options.text: BioPharma, BioAgri, BioServices, and Robotics Biotech
BioAgri, BioPharma, Renewable Energy, and BioMedical

solution:
The correct answer is __**BioPharma, BioIndustrial, BioAgri, and BioServices**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India BioEconomy Report (IBER) 2025**, as highlighted by **GS Krishnan**, the **President** of the **Association of Biotechnology Led Enterprises (ABLE)**, outlines the massive growth potential of India’s biotechnology sector.
 
• The report identifies four major sectors that constitute the backbone of the Indian bioeconomy: **BioPharma**, **BioIndustrial**, **BioAgri**, and **BioServices**.
 
• The **BioPharma** sector remains the largest contributor, driven by India's strengths in **vaccine manufacturing**, **diagnostics**, and **therapeutics**.
 
• **BioIndustrial** applications focus on sustainable solutions, including the production of **bio-fuels**, **industrial enzymes**, and **bio-plastics** to meet environmental goals.
 
• The **BioAgri** segment emphasizes **genetically modified (GM) seeds**, **bio-fertilizers**, and **bio-pesticides** to enhance agricultural yield and food security.
 
• **BioServices** involves **Contract Research Organizations (CROs)** and **Contract Development and Manufacturing Organizations (CDMOs)**, providing clinical trial and research services to global partners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Economic Targets:** The Indian bioeconomy is projected to reach a valuation of **$150 billion** by **2025** and aims for a long-term goal of **$300 billion** by **2030**.
 
• **Global Standing:** India is currently ranked among the **top 12** biotechnology destinations in the world and holds the **3rd** position in the **Asia-Pacific** region.
 
• **BioPharma Dominance:** Within the bioeconomy, **BioPharma** accounts for nearly **49% to 50%** of the total share, largely due to India's role as the "Pharmacy of the World."
 
• **Startup Ecosystem:** The number of biotech startups in India has grown exponentially, surpassing **6,000** enterprises, supported by government initiatives like **Startup India**.
 
• **Bio-Services Growth:** This sector is growing rapidly as global pharmaceutical companies outsource **R&D** and **clinical trials** to India due to cost-efficiency and a highly skilled workforce.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Support:** The **Department of Biotechnology (DBT)** and the **Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC)** are instrumental in providing funding and infrastructure to the industry.
 
• **Bio-IT and Data:** While not a primary pillar like the four mentioned, **Bio-IT** and **Bioinformatics** are emerging as critical enablers for drug discovery and personalized medicine.
 
• **Sustainability:** The **BioIndustrial** sector is aligned with India’s **Net Zero** targets, specifically through the **Ethanol Blending Programme** and the development of **Second-Generation (2G) Bio-refineries**.
 
• **Geographic Hubs:** Major biotechnology clusters have been established in **Bengaluru**, **Hyderabad**, **Pune**, and the **National Capital Region (NCR)** to foster innovation.
 
• **Yearly Performance:** In the year **2023**, the bioeconomy was valued at approximately **$137 billion**, showing a robust year-on-year growth exceeding **10%**.
